original_question: Find a direct reduction from the three-dimensional nonlinear Schrodinger equation to the one-dimensional nonlinear Schrodinger equation through singular solutions, and similarly relate the three-dimensional compressible Euler equation to singular solutions supported on one-dimensional submanifolds.
target_in_paper: Problem 35 in Section 13 ("Singular vorticities in the Euler equation", p. 26), read together with the NLS/compressible-fluid context supplied in Section 14 ("The compressible Euler equation and the NLS equation", p. 27).
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper's specific open problem: a 3D-to-1D reduction for the nonlinear Schrödinger equation via singular solutions, together with the analogous question for the 3D compressible Euler equations and singular solutions supported on one-dimensional submanifolds.
missing_details: The paper asks for a direct link from the 3D NLS to the 1D NLS specifically without passing through the localized induction approximation (LIA).

The nearby context explains the existing indirect route: LIA for curve-supported vorticity in 3D yields the binormal (vortex-filament) equation, and that equation is related to the 1D NLS via the Hasimoto transform.
The 3D NLS is referred to in the paper as the Gross–Pitaevskii (or 3D NLS) equation.

On the compressible-fluid side, the analogous target is a reduction from the 3D compressible Euler equations to singular solutions supported on 1D submanifolds, i.e. curve-supported singular solutions.

Section 14 supplies the intended hydrodynamic context by recalling the Madelung transform between a barotropic-type fluid system and the NLS; your draft does not mention that NLS/compressible-fluid linkage.
No algebraic data such as ambient field, homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, or asymptotic quantifiers appear in this problem; the missing details are geometric and procedural instead.
refined_question: Find a direct link between the three-dimensional Gross–Pitaevskii/nonlinear Schrödinger equation and the one-dimensional nonlinear Schrödinger equation by realizing the 1D equation as a reduction to singular filament-type solutions of the 3D equation, rather than obtaining it indirectly through the localized induction approximation and the binormal/Hasimoto route. Formulate the analogous reduction for the three-dimensional compressible Euler equations, namely a reduction to singular solutions supported on one-dimensional submanifolds.
justification: The draft is essentially a paraphrase of Problem 35, which is the paper's exact open problem on this topic. Section 13 sets the scope by recalling that the localized induction approximation for 3D Euler vorticity concentrated on curves produces the binormal equation, that this equation is related to the 1D NLS via the Hasimoto transform, and that it also gives singular solutions of the Gross–Pitaevskii/3D NLS equation. Problem 35 then asks for a direct 3D-NLS-to-1D-NLS link via singular solutions, explicitly bypassing LIA, and states the analogous question for the 3D compressible Euler equations with singular solutions supported on 1D submanifolds. Section 14 is the relevant nearby context because it explains the paper's intended NLS/compressible-fluid correspondence through the Madelung transform and the associated barotropic-type fluid system. There is no theorem or proposition in the paper giving an official equivalent restatement of Problem 35, so the refined question should stay in open-problem form and remain narrowly focused on this direct reduction.
